details.body: In crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs, `CRITICAL_MOLT_GH_RATIO` (line 12, value 0.3) is a file-level `const` that determines when molts unconditionally fail (GH < 30% of gh_min_d). The acceptance criteria require 'All molt-related thresholds and modifiers are named parameters in species/process data, not hardcoded constants.' Move this to a field on `ShrimpRuntimeParams` (e.g., `critical_molt_gh_ratio: f64` with default 0.3) and add a corresponding optional field in `ShrimpPreset`.

Current-schema save/load can advance newly added shrimp halfway through the molt cycle. AnimalState still defaults inter_molt_timer_days to 14.0 (crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:615), AddShrimp seeds the adult stage timer to 0 without syncing that legacy field (crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:818-823), and normalize_loaded_shrimp_reproduction_state() blindly backfills any all-zero stage timers from inter_molt_timer_days (crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:946-960). A fresh v13 save with newly added adults will therefore reload with adult.molt_timer_days = 14.0 instead of 0. Restrict that backfill to migrated pre-v13 payloads, or only run it when the stage timer fields were absent in the source JSON.

Cold-water molt failures are misreported. molt_cycle() multiplies success by temp_condition_factor() for both below- and above-optimal temperatures (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:440-441, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:504-506), but emit_molt_failure() and emit_molt_stress_warning() only add a temperature cause when temperature_c > optimal_temp_max_c (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1113-1118, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1161-1163). In a cold tank, the new mechanic can fail molts while emitting only PoorCondition, which hides the actual driver. Add an explicit low-temperature cause/detail, or at minimum include any non-optimal temperature penalty in the event summary.

Reserve depletion is part of the new success formula, but it is not surfaced in failure diagnostics. The success path feeds reserve_g into molt_condition_modifier() (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:502-503, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1258-1276), yet emit_molt_failure() only reports a raw condition index when it blames PoorCondition (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1120-1127). A reserve-driven failure can therefore log a seemingly healthy condition value with no reserve/starvation hint. Include reserve-per-shrimp or reserve shortfall in the event details, or emit a starvation/reserve cause code when that branch drives the failure.

The ‘very low GH forces failure’ cutoff is still a hidden magic threshold. CRITICAL_MOLT_GH_RATIO is hardcoded at 0.3 (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:12) and applied directly in the failure gate (crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:439, crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:508) instead of coming from ShrimpRuntimeParams. That leaves one of the new molt-failure boundaries untunable and without preset/provenance coverage. Promote this cutoff into named runtime/preset data, or derive it from the existing named GH parameters rather than keeping a hidden constant.

Fix failing test `test_salt_treatment_emergency_scenario` in `crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs`. The `salt_treatment_source_profile()` helper constructs a `SourceWaterProfile` by copying DIC and alkalinity concentrations from the tank state, but the resulting DIC/alkalinity combination produces a pH that fails `validate_source_water_carbonate_profile()` with `InvalidSourceProfile { field: "carbonate_derived_ph", value: 8.5 }`. The source profile needs its DIC and alkalinity values adjusted (or a valid carbonate equilibrium explicitly set) so the profile passes validation when inserted into the source water catalog.

In `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs`, the `molt_cycle` function also has a legacy-timer fallback (lines 508-523) that duplicates the migration logic in `save.rs:normalize_loaded_shrimp_reproduction_state`. With the new schema version guard in save.rs (only applying the fallback for `source_schema_version < PER_STAGE_MOLT_TIMER_SCHEMA_VERSION`), the runtime fallback in `molt_cycle` remains unconditional and will silently override zero stage timers from `inter_molt_timer_days` even on schema-14 saves. Consider whether the runtime fallback should also be guarded or removed, since its presence means the migration fix in save.rs is partially dead code for the runtime path.

Fix [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-151]: the rewritten emergency scenario no longer proves that chloride protection is what lowered mortality. The helper at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-88] builds replacement water from `WaterState::default_for_volume_l(1.0)` ([crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-109]), so the 50% water change also reduces TAN/DOC/DON and changes alkalinity, DIC, and DO, while the assertion at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:109-151] compares pre-treatment vs post-treatment mortality inside the same evolving run instead of against a matched control. In a local probe, that assertion still held with `chloride_protection_factor = 0.0`, so this test can pass even if chloride protection itself is broken. Use a parallel untreated/control tank, or a second water-change control that keeps every field identical except chloride/sodium, so the test actually guards the chloride-specific mechanic.
